blocks.content:
Doctrine of Basic Structure:
• Established in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).
• Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

Doctrine of Judicial Review:
• Courts can invalidate unconstitutional laws.
Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

rows: Limits Parliament from altering the basic structure of the Constitution
Empowers courts to invalidate unconstitutional laws

items: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) is directly linked to the establishment of the Doctrine of Basic Structure.
Judicial Review empowers courts to strike down unconstitutional legislation enacted by Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Doctrine of Basic Structure was established in the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case in 1973.
Under the Basic Structure doctrine, Parliament is restricted from altering fundamental constitutional features.
The Doctrine of Judicial Review grants courts the power to invalidate laws deemed unconstitutional.
